# Wittgenstein — Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (1922)

## Bibliographic identity

Consulted edition: Ludwig Wittgenstein, *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus*, translated by F. P. Ramsey and edited by C. K. Ogden (Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner & Co., 1922). The Ludwig Wittgenstein Project's public digital edition identifies this base edition. Proposition numbers remain stable locators.

**Bibliography:** Wittgenstein, Ludwig. *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus*. Translated by F. P. Ramsey. Edited by C. K. Ogden. Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner & Co., 1922. https://books.wittgensteinproject.org/pdf/english/Tractatus%20Logico-Philosophicus%20%28English%29.pdf.

## Essay use

Primary source for the relation between saying/showing, the ladder at 6.54, and the silence of proposition 7. It places the limits of propositional articulation inside the work's own method.

**Passages needed:** propositions 4.12–4.1212, 6.4–6.522, 6.54, and 7 in the chosen translation.

**Claim boundary:** the source warrants claims about the limit of saying under the *Tractatus*'s own project. The QL reading concerns the structural pressure at that limit; any positive metaphysical development belongs to the essay's further argument.

> What can be shown cannot be said.

- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent, 2026-07-14; PDF text and rendered page checked; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.

- **Consumers:** [[04-s01-p3-formal-limit-genealogy]]; [[06-s01-p5-return-zero]]; [[A03-Immutable-Gap-Formal-Limit]]; [[C64-Paradox-Transforming-the-Containing-Field]]; movement 4 saying/showing comparison and movement 6 saying/showing context.
